description: An account created via CREATE2, self-destructed within the same transaction (fully removed per EIP-6780 since it was created this tx), and then re-deployed at the same address via a second same-tx CREATE2. Verifies that the final SSR reflects a real net account delta (nonexistent -> existing) rather than being omitted by the create-then-destroy pruning rule, since a persistent account DOES remain at the transaction boundary.
spec_gap_note: semantic_contract.md §3.2 only states the omission rule for the create-then-destroy case. This vector is the worked example motivating an explicit 'unless recreated later in the same transaction' clause -- see the note left in that section.

tx_execution_path.note: created this tx, so per EIP-6780 the account is fully deleted (nonce/code/balance zeroed) and its balance transferred
same address is free again since step 2 fully deleted it; second deployment succeeds

code_hash.current: <hash of second deployment's init code output>

account_deltas.reason: a persistent account remains at the transaction boundary, so the create-then-destroy omission rule (semantic_contract.md §3.2) does not apply even though the account was also created+destroyed earlier in this same transaction

notes: Sender balance figure bundles the 5 ETH sent across both CREATE2 endowments plus illustrative gas billing -- not a precisely metered value. An implementation must replace it with real Prague-spec gas accounting. code_hash is left symbolic since it depends on the exact init code chosen for the fixture; fill in a concrete value once a real extractor can compute it.
